title: Universal curve-test datum for a failure
statement:
With $f:X\to S$ and $n$ as in [sbc-def-base-change-property] assume for
some $q\geq1$ that $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q')$ holds universally for all
$q'\leq q-1$, but $\mathrm{BC}(f,n,q)$ does not hold universally. Then there exist a commutative diagram

$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X & \longleftarrow & X' & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \longleftarrow & S' & \longleftarrow & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

with both squares Cartesian, where

1. $S'$ is affine, integral, and normal with algebraically closed
function field;
1. $K$ is algebraically closed and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ is
dominant (in other words $K$ is an extension of the function
field of $S'$),

and there exists an integer $d\mid n$ such that
$R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)$ is nonzero.
(*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.88.7, [Tag `0F08`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F08).*)

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-bc-failure-field] to obtain an affine $S_0$, a base change $f_0:X_0\to S_0$, a field $K_0$, $g_0:\operatorname{Spec}K_0\to S_0$, and an $n$-annihilated sheaf $F_0$ whose degree-$q$ base-change arrow is not an isomorphism. The cumulative universal hypothesis includes every degree required by that lemma. Both schemes at the ends of $g_0$ are affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) gives that $g_0$ is qcqs.

Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $K_0$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The map $\rho:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}K_0$ is integral: each element of an algebraic field extension satisfies a monic equation after dividing by the leading coefficient; both spectra have one point, so it is surjective. Pull back the fibre square and set $F=\rho^{-1}F_0$, still killed by $n$. By [sbc-lem-bc-integral-surjective], an isomorphism for the composite $g= g_0\circ\rho$ and $F$ would imply an isomorphism for $g_0,F_0$, a contradiction. Its hypothesis is exactly the universal degree-$q-1$ hypothesis; no arbitrary extension is being asserted integral.

Apply [lem-sbc-normalization-algclosed-field] to $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S_0$. Obtain $\pi:S'\to S_0$ integral, $S'$ affine integral normal with algebraically closed function field $L$, and $g':\operatorname{Spec}K\to S'$ induced by $L\hookrightarrow K$, with $g=\pi\circ g'$. Put $X'=X_0\times_{S_0}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}\operatorname{Spec}K$. The resulting squares paste to base changes of the original $f$. The map $g'$ is qcqs by the affine-scheme and morphism-permanence nodes. Apply [lem-sbc-integral-pushforward-base-change-arrow]: if the new arrow were an isomorphism, its integral pushforward, identified there with the old arrow, would be an isomorphism, contradicting step 2. Thus failure survives normalization.

Universal degree-$q-1$ base change remains valid for $f'$ by the definition of universality: a further base change of $f'$ is a base change of $f$, since the Cartesian squares paste. Apply [sbc-lem-bc-injectivity](1) to $g'$ and $F$. The new degree-$q$ arrow is a monomorphism and is not an isomorphism. Its target $R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ is therefore nonzero: a monomorphism to the zero object has zero source, in which case the arrow is the isomorphism between two zero objects. Moreover $h$ is qcqs as a base change of $g'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3).

Set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$; $n\geq1$ by [sbc-def-base-change-property]. Since $nF=0$, scalar multiplication $[a]x=ax$ equips $F$ with its canonical $\Lambda$-module structure. Inverse image retains this action, and the target of [sbc-def-base-change-map] is $H^q(Rh_*Le^*(F[0]))$. Apply [lem-sbc-coefficient-higher-direct-image-zero] to $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$, the qcqs map $h$, and $e^{-1}F$: its underlying abelian higher direct image is the nonzero object of step 4, so its $\Lambda$-module higher direct image is nonzero. Now [lem-sbc-prime-cyclic-detection] applies with $K$ algebraically closed, $n\ne0$, $n=0$ in $\Lambda$ and $h$ qcqs. It supplies a prime $r\mid n$ and a nonzero $R^qh_*\underline{P_r/(r)}$, where $P_r=\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf F_r)$.

In $P_r$ multiplication by $r$ is zero, so $P_r/(r)\cong P_r$, whose underlying additive group is canonically $\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sbc-coefficient-higher-direct-image-zero] to $\mathbf Z\to P_r$ and the constant sheaf $P_r/(r)$: nonzero higher direct image in $P_r$-modules is equivalent to nonzero underlying abelian higher direct image. Constant sheafification preserves the displayed additive isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Consequently $R^qh_*\underline{\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z}\ne0$. Take $d=r$, retaining the divisibility witness from step 5 and the two Cartesian squares of step 3. This yields all the clauses of the statement. In particular no identification of $\Lambda/(r)$ with $\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$ for an arbitrary ring is used.
